svg.title: Two agents, one set of blocks
svg.desc: The sleep-time set-up of Letta, as a timeline of ten turns. Top lane: the primary agent answers each user message; it reads the memory blocks, can search past messages, and has no tool to edit the blocks. Bottom lane: the sleep-time agent runs in the background after turns 5 and 10, by default, reads the messages since its last run, and edits the shared blocks with memory_insert, memory_replace or memory_rethink, then memory_finish_edits. A fact the user states in turn 2 reaches the blocks only when the sleep-time agent runs after turn 5; until then it is only in the conversation.
svg.text: Two agents, one set of blocks
With a sleep-time agent, the agent that answers cannot write, and a second agent edits the shared blocks in the
background, every few turns. The user never waits for it.
Letta's default: the sleep-time agent runs every fifth turn
The sleep-time agent has its own prompt, which asks for specific dates in place of “today” or “recently”. The notebook runs it once after each
session, the simplest set-up that shows the same mechanism.
